title: the WSG natural hazards opener slice - the volcano eruption types with the 1d4 lava bands, the 1d6 ash bands and the explosive cloudkill, the earthquake classes from light through severe, and the tidal wave approach rules, printed pp. 76-79
audit_label: R486 WSG natural hazards pin audit
audit_comment: The natural hazards opener: three types of volcanic eruption, each volcano locked to one type - lava, ash, or explosive. Lava: magma inside, lava expelled; fluid magma sprays less violently, side fissures dissipate but never eliminate the crater flow; lava incinerates combustibles even barely flowing, and after it stops retains serious-burn heat for 2d3 weeks; a mobile character almost certainly avoids the 250-yards-per-hour flow, but the pyroclastic bombs and blocks are the greater danger. The 1d4 lava bands: 1-2 fluid magma for 2d6 days, 1d6 damage per turn within 500 yards, a 50-degree rise one quarter mile out tapering 10 degrees per quarter mile to nothing at 1.5 miles; 3 thick magma for 2d4 days, 1d4 per turn within 500 yards, a 30-degree rise dying at 1 mile; 4 thick magma plus pyroclastics - 1 percent per hour within 1000 yards, 2d6 from a hit, plus 5 percent and 1d6 per 100 yards closer. Ash: overshadowed lava, seldom violent past the initial blast; the 2000-3000 foot opaque cloud, lighter ash carried dozens of miles settling 3-4 inches; ash kills green plants yet is a supreme fertilizer; St. Helens 1980-1981, six incidents over 10 months, superheated-gas snowmelt mudslides over 100,000 acres, the May 18 1980 blast equal to 10 megatons flattening trees 4 miles out, the peak dropping from 9,677 to 8,364 feet. The 1d6 ash bands: 1-3 light to moderate, at least 12 hours daily for 1d4+2 weeks, 2 inches at 1d10+15 miles downwind, 6 inches within 1d6+4 miles, 1d3 burn per turn within 2000 yards unless sheltered, save versus breath weapon each turn against a choking fit (-4 to hit, +4 to be hit), two straight failures meaning 1d4 per round and death inside one turn without aid; 4-5 heavy, 1d6+5 hours daily for 1d3 weeks, significant ash at 1d6+9 miles, 9 inches within 1d6+2 miles, the danger zone widening to 4000 yards; 6 heavy plus pyroclastics for the first 3-8 days. Explosive: the opening salvo blows the top off, the peak collapsing into the magma chamber; sight range is mortal danger - the ash cloud and the 3-5-mile glowing avalanche exude double-strength cloudkill, half a round of breath slaying below 8+1 hit dice, 8+1 through 10+1 saving at -4, above saving normally; 1d3 days of ash puffs, lava leaks and tremors warn first. Earthquakes: fault-line pressure, shock waves outdamaging the shift, quakes triggering quakes, aftershocks for days, wilderness scope only. Light: seconds of shiver, no direct harm, but spells ruined, the jostled trap-working thief failing 50 percent of the time, the tightrope walker halved and falling without a Dexterity Check. Moderate: 10-15 seconds (d6+9), 20 percent shorter, 30 percent longer to 30; dislodges from precarious perches, the straddled limb needing both Dexterity and Strength, Climbing at -50 percent, the specialist missile at -2 save point blank, the non-specialist at -3, -5 and -7, melee at -3 with the slip-and-fall on a miss, rockfall or mudslide at the cliff base, the 1-in-8 uprooted tree, the fissure with falling, abrasion and crush. Severe: everything doubled, Climbing -100 percent, melee -6, the rockfall chance twice as great, 40-90 seconds, hit the ground. Tidal waves: born of undersea cataclysm, the ocean absorbing and passing on the shock for thousands of miles; sighted half a mile out, at least 150 mph, less than 30 seconds of warning, at least 75 feet by 500 feet, almost 30 million gallons; rushing inland several miles at 20 mph, the 5,000-foot cliff sparing those hundreds of yards back while the 20-mile lowland fears as much as the coast; the direct-path victim dies. The section cuts mid-sentence at the page bottom - the death-rule continuation rides with R487.

banner.title: R486: the WSG NATURAL HAZARDS opener slice, printed pp. 76-79 - opening the natural hazards chapter in one content-density round: the volcano frame with the one-type rule, the lava general rules with the 250-yd/hr flow and the 2d3-week heat retention, the 1d4 lava bands (fluid 2d6 days with the 50-degree taper, thick 2d4 days with the 30-degree taper, pyroclastic with the 1-percent base and the 5-and-1d6-per-100-yards escalation), the ash cloud and fertilizer rules with the Mount St. Helens account, the 1d6 ash bands (light 1d4+2 weeks with the 1d3-burn and breath-weapon choke chain, heavy 1d6+5 hours with the 4000-yard danger zone, six with the 3-8-day pyroclastic spell), the explosive cloudkill bands with the 1d3-day warning, the light, moderate and severe quake classes with the doubling rule, and the tidal wave approach rules through the direct-path death - the section cut mid-sentence at the p. 79 bottom rides with R487.
banner.provenance: THE SETTLE: two-way clean on the first pass - the tesseract full-text reads, the pdfy layout read and the tsv coordinate reads agree on every number of all four pages (the 250-yd/hr flow, the 2d3 weeks, the 50/30-degree rises with the 10-degree taper, the 500/2000/4000-yard danger radii, the 2000-3000 foot ash cloud, the 9,677 to 8,364 foot St. Helens peak, all the 1d4+2 and 1d10+15 style dice, the d6+9 and 1d6+3-tens quake durations, and the 150 mph, 75-foot, 500-foot, 30-second wave). The garbles all settled without contest: the tesseract 17/ and the pdfy 1V2 both read 1.5 miles, the /s and V4 mile reads are the one-quarter-mile reference distance, the tesseract underatreehasa1in 8 is under a tree has a 1 in 8, the book's own crevasse spelling stands, and the (1d6 +3) beside 40-90 seconds is tens-of-seconds die notation. Printed p. 79 ends mid-sentence at and he will - the tidal wave death-rule continuation rides with R487, and the tidal waves gap box stays open until then.
banner.sentinel: Bounds held: the 1d4 lava and 1d6 ash bands tile their dice exactly, the danger radii ascend 500 to 2000 to 4000 yards, both temperature rises are exact multiples of the quarter-mile taper closing at 1.5 and 1 mile, the severe quake exactly doubles the moderate penalties, the cloudkill hit-die bands abut at 8+1 and 10+1, the ash accumulations ascend 2 to 6 to 9 inches, and the 150-mph wave sighted at half a mile fits inside the 30-second warning bound.

consts.name: whzVolcanoEruptionTypes
consts.comment: three types of volcanic eruption for game purposes: lava, ash, explosive

consts.name: whzLavaHeatWeeksMin
consts.comment: even after it stops flowing and looks cooled, the lava retains serious-burn heat for 2d3 weeks: minimum 2

consts.name: whzLavaHeatWeeksMax
consts.comment: the 2d3-week heat retention maximum

consts.name: whzLavaFlowYardsPerHour
consts.comment: a speed of 250 yards per hour is about average for a lava flow, and it does not usually gush forth in massive quantities at one time

consts.name: whzFluidLavaDaysMin
consts.comment: 1d4 result 1-2, fluid magma: the eruption spews for 2d6 days, minimum 2

consts.name: whzFluidLavaDaysMax
consts.comment: the 2d6-day fluid eruption maximum

consts.name: whzFluidLavaHeatDmgDie
consts.comment: fluid magma: a character closer than 500 yards to a significant source takes at least 1d6 points of damage per turn from radiant heat, possibly much more when considerably closer

consts.name: whzFluidTempRiseDeg
consts.comment: fluid magma: the effective air temperature one-quarter mile from the site increases by 50 degrees for as long as the eruption continues, much more in close proximity

consts.name: whzLavaHeatRangeYards
consts.comment: the radiant-heat damage range for both the fluid and the thick bands: closer than 500 yards to a significant source or sizable quantity

consts.name: whzLavaTempTaperDeg
consts.comment: the fluid and thick temperature increases taper off by 10 degrees per additional quarter mile of distance from the site

consts.name: whzFluidNoHeatQmi
consts.comment: fluid magma: no heat difference is detectable from 1.5 miles away - six quarter-miles from the site

consts.name: whzThickLavaDaysMin
consts.comment: 1d4 result 3, thick magma: sprays into the air and flows out around the crater mouth for 2d4 days, minimum 2

consts.name: whzThickLavaDaysMax
consts.comment: the 2d4-day thick eruption maximum

consts.name: whzThickLavaHeatDmgDie
consts.comment: thick magma: a character closer than 500 yards to a sizable quantity suffers at least 1d4 points of damage per turn

consts.name: whzThickTempRiseDeg
consts.comment: thick magma: the effective air temperature one-quarter mile from the site increases by 30 degrees

consts.name: whzThickNoHeatQmi
consts.comment: thick magma: no heat difference is felt from 1 mile away - four quarter-miles

consts.name: whzPyroclasticRangeYards
consts.comment: 1d4 result 4, thick magma plus pyroclastic material: a character within 1,000 yards of the site is subject to the falling bombs and blocks

consts.name: whzPyroclasticHitChancePct
consts.comment: a 1 percent chance per hour of being hit by one or more chunks of pyroclastic material

consts.name: whzPyroclasticDmgMin
consts.comment: a pyroclastic hit costs 2d6 hit points from burn and impact damage, minimum 2

consts.name: whzPyroclasticDmgMax
consts.comment: the 2d6-point pyroclastic hit maximum

consts.name: whzPyroclasticStepYards
consts.comment: for every 100 yards of distance less than 1,000 yards from the site

consts.name: whzPyroclasticChanceStepPct
consts.comment: each 100 yards closer increases the hourly hit chance by 5 percent

consts.name: whzPyroclasticDmgStepDie
consts.comment: each 100 yards closer increases the damage from a hit by 1d6

consts.name: whzAshCloudHeightMinFt
consts.comment: the original ash cloud can easily be 2,000 or 3,000 feet high directly above the mouth of the volcano

consts.name: whzAshCloudHeightMaxFt
consts.comment: the original cloud height upper figure

consts.name: whzAshFarAccumInchesMin
consts.comment: even dozens of miles out, the accumulation on solid surfaces can be as great as three or four inches over an average-length eruption of moderate intensity

consts.name: whzAshFarAccumInchesMax
consts.comment: the far accumulation upper figure

consts.name: whzStHelensYear
consts.comment: the Mount St. Helens eruption occurred during 1980 and 1981

consts.name: whzStHelensIncidents
consts.comment: actually six separate incidents over a 10-month period

consts.name: whzStHelensMonths
consts.comment: the six incidents spanned 10 months

consts.name: whzStHelensMudslideAcres
consts.comment: the mudslides covered more than 100,000 acres of land in the vicinity

consts.name: whzStHelensBlastMegatons
consts.comment: the initial blast on May 18, 1980 had a force equal to a 10-megaton hydrogen bomb

consts.name: whzStHelensTreesMiles
consts.comment: the concussive force knocked over trees as far as 4 miles away

consts.name: whzStHelensBeforeFt
consts.comment: the peak of Mount St. Helens was 9,677 feet above sea level before the eruption

consts.name: whzStHelensAfterFt
consts.comment: and only 8,364 feet when the last expulsion of ash subsided

consts.name: whzAshLightDailyHours
consts.comment: 1d6 result 1-3, light to moderate but extended: ash is expelled for at least 12 hours each day

consts.name: whzAshLightWeeksMin
consts.comment: for a period of 1d4+2 weeks, minimum 3

consts.name: whzAshLightWeeksMax
consts.comment: the 1d4+2-week duration maximum

consts.name: whzAshLightFarAccumInches
consts.comment: a significant amount of ash, at least 2 inches of total accumulation, is carried downwind

consts.name: whzAshLightFarMilesMin
consts.comment: the significant ash settles 1d10+15 miles from the site in the direction of the prevailing winds, minimum 16

consts.name: whzAshLightFarMilesMax
consts.comment: the 1d10+15-mile downwind maximum

consts.name: whzAshLightNearAccumInches
consts.comment: heavier amounts of ash, 6 inches or more, settle everywhere within the near radius

consts.name: whzAshLightNearMilesMin
consts.comment: the heavy accumulation falls within a radius of 1d6+4 miles of the site, minimum 5

consts.name: whzAshLightNearMilesMax
consts.comment: the 1d6+4-mile near radius maximum

consts.name: whzAshLightDangerYards
consts.comment: a character within 2,000 yards of the eruption site suffers the burn damage

consts.name: whzAshBurnDmgDie
consts.comment: 1d3 points of burn damage per turn from the hot particles that settle on his body

consts.name: whzChokeAtkPenalty
consts.comment: in a choking fit: -4 on attack rolls

consts.name: whzChokeBeHitBonus
consts.comment: in a choking fit: +4 to be hit

consts.name: whzAsphyxDmgDie
consts.comment: the asphyxiating character takes 1d4 points of damage per round

consts.name: whzAshHeavyHoursMin
consts.comment: 1d6 result 4-5, heavy but relatively short: ash is expelled 1d6+5 hours each day, minimum 6

consts.name: whzAshHeavyHoursMax
consts.comment: the 1d6+5 daily-hours maximum

consts.name: whzAshHeavyWeeksMin
consts.comment: for a period of 1d3 weeks, minimum 1

consts.name: whzAshHeavyWeeksMax
consts.comment: the 1d3-week duration maximum

consts.name: whzAshHeavyFarMilesMin
consts.comment: a significant amount of ash accumulates 1d6+9 miles away from the site in the direction of the wind, minimum 10

consts.name: whzAshHeavyFarMilesMax
consts.comment: the 1d6+9-mile downwind maximum

consts.name: whzAshHeavyNearAccumInches
consts.comment: a heavy accumulation of 9 inches or more comes down everywhere within the near radius

consts.name: whzAshHeavyNearMilesMin
consts.comment: the heavy accumulation falls within a radius of 1d6+2 miles of the site, minimum 3

consts.name: whzAshHeavyNearMilesMax
consts.comment: the 1d6+2-mile near radius maximum

consts.name: whzAshHeavyDangerYards
consts.comment: the heavy-band danger zone for characters is 4,000 yards

consts.name: whzAshSixPyrDaysMin
consts.comment: 1d6 result 6, the first 3-8 days of the heavy eruption are marked by the expulsion of pyroclastic material, minimum 3

consts.name: whzAshSixPyrDaysMax
consts.comment: the pyroclastic spell of band 6 lasts at most 8 days

consts.name: whzGlowingAvalancheMilesMin
consts.comment: a glowing avalanche of thick lava and heavy ash flows from the newly enlarged mouth, threatening to incinerate and then inundate anything within a radius of 3-5 miles, minimum 3

consts.name: whzGlowingAvalancheMilesMax
consts.comment: the glowing-avalanche radius maximum

consts.name: whzCloudkillStrength
consts.comment: the ash cloud or the avalanche, or both, exude superheated air and noxious gases with the effect of a double-strength cloudkill spell

consts.name: whzCloudkillSlaysBelowHd
consts.comment: the cloudkill slays fewer than 8+1 hit dice - 9 hit dice and below

consts.name: whzCloudkillMidSavePenalty
consts.comment: those with 8+1 to 10+1 hit dice must save versus poison at -4

consts.name: whzCloudkillMidMaxHd
consts.comment: those with more than 10+1 hit dice - 11 and above - must save versus poison normally to avoid death

consts.name: whzExplosiveWarningDaysMax
consts.comment: the warning signs continue for 1d3 days before the eruption begins with full force - anyone who remains despite them gets what he deserves

consts.name: whzQuakeClasses
consts.comment: for game purposes earthquakes are classified as light, moderate, or severe

consts.name: whzLightQuakeThiefFailPct
consts.comment: the jostled thief has a 50 percent chance to fail even if an earlier dice roll indicated he would succeed

consts.name: whzModQuakeSecMin
consts.comment: a moderate quake normally lasts d6+9 seconds, minimum 10

consts.name: whzModQuakeSecMax
consts.comment: the d6+9-second moderate duration maximum

consts.name: whzModQuakeLessPct
consts.comment: occasionally (20 percent) a moderate quake lasts less than the normal duration

consts.name: whzModQuakeMorePct
consts.comment: sometimes (30 percent) more, up to 25 or 30 seconds

consts.name: whzModQuakeMoreSecMax
consts.comment: the occasional long moderate quake tops out at 30 seconds

consts.name: whzModQuakeClimbPenaltyPct
consts.comment: someone climbing a severe or moderate slope must make a Climbing Check at a -50 percent penalty to his Climbing Rating to avoid losing his footing and tumbling down the slope

consts.name: whzModQuakeSpecMissilePenalty
consts.comment: a character specialized in a missile weapon takes a -2 penalty to hit if he gets a shot off during a moderate quake

consts.name: whzModQuakeNonSpecShort
consts.comment: a non-specialist with a missile weapon takes -3 to hit at short range

consts.name: whzModQuakeNonSpecMed
consts.comment: a -5 penalty at medium range

consts.name: whzModQuakeNonSpecLong
consts.comment: and a -7 penalty at long range

consts.name: whzModQuakeMeleePenalty
consts.comment: any character in melee combat takes a -3 penalty on all attack rolls

consts.name: whzModQuakeTreeFallChance
consts.comment: a character standing under a tree has a 1-in-8 chance of being hit if the tree is uprooted and falls

consts.name: whzSevQuakeClimbPenaltyPct
consts.comment: the Climbing Rating penalty is -100 percent instead of -50

consts.name: whzSevQuakeMeleePenalty
consts.comment: the melee attack-roll penalty is -6 instead of -3

consts.name: whzSevQuakeSecMin
consts.comment: a severe quake lasts 1d6+3 tens of seconds - 40 to 90 seconds, minimum 40

consts.name: whzSevQuakeSecMax
consts.comment: the severe duration maximum

consts.name: whzTidalSightHalfMiles
consts.comment: a character within sight of the shore and looking out to sea will notice the oncoming wall of water when it is one-half mile away from the shore

consts.name: whzTidalMinMph
consts.comment: the velocity of the wave will be at least 150 miles per hour

consts.name: whzTidalMaxWarnSec
consts.comment: even in the best case less than 30 seconds pass from the time it is sighted until it hits the shore

consts.name: whzTidalMinHeightFt
consts.comment: the wave will be at least 75 feet tall

consts.name: whzTidalLengthFt
consts.comment: and 500 feet long when it hits

consts.name: whzTidalVolumeMillionGal
consts.comment: which translates to a volume of almost 30 million gallons for the smallest tidal wave possible

consts.name: whzTidalInlandMph
consts.comment: the diminished inland velocity of the several million gallons still moving

consts.name: whzTidalCliffFt
consts.comment: if an ocean ends at the base of a cliff rising 5,000 feet above the water

consts.name: whzTidalLowlandMiles
consts.comment: but if the terrain 20 miles inland is still only a few feet above sea level

bools.name: whzOneTypePerVolcano
bools.comment: any single volcano always erupts in only one of the three types - it will not spout a lava eruption one time and an ash eruption the next

bools.name: whzDormantAwakensFast
bools.comment: a volcano can lie dormant so long it is forgotten even in local legends, then in the space of days or even hours come alive and unleash all its fury

bools.name: whzPerpetuallyActive
bools.comment: other volcanoes are almost perpetually active, spitting out a bit of ash and smoke every few weeks as a reminder

bools.name: whzMagmaInsideLavaOut
bools.comment: the molten rock is properly called magma when inside the volcano and lava after it is expelled

bools.name: whzLavaSpraysWhenThick
bools.comment: the red-hot liquid can spray out of the center of the crater if forced out by fairly high pressure from beneath and if the molten rock is relatively thick

bools.name: whzFluidMagmaLessViolent
bools.comment: the more fluid the magma beneath the surface, the less violent the explosion when it is propelled up to the surface

bools.name: whzLavaSideFissures
bools.comment: some lava finds its way out through fissures in the sides, which dissipates the force of the eruption out of the crater mouth but does not eliminate the possibility of a crater flow

bools.name: whzLavaTopAndSides
bools.comment: lava can come out of the top and the sides of a volcano at the same time

bools.name: whzLavaIncinerates
bools.comment: lava incinerates any combustible object it comes into contact with, even after it has cooled so much that it is barely still flowing

bools.name: whzLavaAvoidable
bools.comment: a character capable of movement and in control of his faculties can almost certainly avoid flowing lava even a short distance from the source

bools.name: whzPyroclasticBombsBlocks
bools.comment: the greater danger near a lava eruption is the expulsion of pyroclastic material - bombs and blocks, blobs of semi-hardened magma and chunks of rock carried along in the upward flow, thrown high and far by the force of the eruption

bools.name: whzAshEruptionsExpelLava
bools.comment: volcanoes with ash eruptions can and often do expel some lava at the same time, but the molten rock is overshadowed by huge clouds of thick hot ash

bools.name: whzAshSeldomViolent
bools.comment: aside from the initial blast that begins the eruption, ash volcanoes are seldom violent - the danger comes from the enormous amount of ash, dust and minuscule lava particles, not explosive force or heat

bools.name: whzAshCloudOpaque
bools.comment: the original cloud is so thick that one cannot see into it, much less through it

bools.name: whzAshLighterCarriedFar
bools.comment: the lighter particles can be carried by the wind for dozens of miles before settling to the ground

bools.name: whzAshKillsPlants
bools.comment: the ash chokes and kills any green plant life that receives even a moderate dusting

bools.name: whzAshFertilizer
bools.comment: the chemical composition of volcanic ash makes it one of nature's best fertilizers - within a few months the slopes are again covered with plants thriving on the rich soil that killed their predecessors

bools.name: whzStHelensWasAshEruption
bools.comment: the eruption of Mount St. Helens in the northwestern United States was an ash eruption

bools.name: whzStHelensSnowmeltMudslides
bools.comment: the superheated gas expelled from the summit melted the surrounding snow cover, leading to mudslides

bools.name: whzStHelensPeakPulverized
bools.comment: the entire time the volcano remained active the summit was pulverized

bools.name: whzAshShelterProtects
bools.comment: unless the character is in a shelter or otherwise protected

bools.name: whzChokeSaveBreathWeapon
bools.comment: such a character must make a saving throw versus breath weapon once per turn to avoid going into a choking fit

bools.name: whzChokeTwoFailsAsphyxiate
bools.comment: a character who fails two saving throws in succession is in danger of being asphyxiated or suffocated

bools.name: whzAsphyxAidWithinTurn
bools.comment: and will die unless he can receive aid within one turn

bools.name: whzAshHeavyUnprotectedEffects
bools.comment: with the light-band effects upon those who are unprotected and within the heavy danger zone

bools.name: whzExplosiveBlowsTop
bools.comment: an explosive eruption cannot be characterized in general terms, but the opening salvo can be strong enough to literally blow the top off the volcano

bools.name: whzExplosivePeakCollapses
bools.comment: a volume of several million cubic feet of rock around the crater mouth cracks and crumbles, and the peak collapses into the chamber of magma or ash (or both) beneath the surface

bools.name: whzExplosiveSightRangeDanger
bools.comment: any characters or creatures within sight range of an explosive eruption are in mortal danger from a variety of sources: a huge cloud of ash and pyroclastic material raining down on the countryside

bools.name: whzExplosiveCloudkillBreath
bools.comment: breathing the air for as little as one-half round slays anything with fewer than 8+1 hit dice

bools.name: whzExplosiveWarnsFirst
bools.comment: an explosive eruption gives sufficient warning first: the volcano puffs out small ash clouds, leaks small amounts of lava, and perhaps sends moderate tremors through the ground

bools.name: whzQuakeOnlyAvoidedByAir
bools.comment: when the earth moves nothing can stand its ground - the only way to avoid an earthquake is to take to the air at just the right time

bools.name: whzQuakeMostlyHarmless
bools.comment: earthquakes do not occur very often, those that do are generally confined to small areas, and the vast majority strong enough to be noticeable are not strong enough to do any harm

bools.name: whzQuakeWildernessScope
bools.comment: this discussion is limited to quakes in wilderness areas with no stable human or humanoid populations, since the book's scope does not include cities and villages

bools.name: whzQuakeFaultLines
bools.comment: most earthquakes occur along fault lines, where two sections of bedrock come together and exert pressure against each other - the DM places the fault lines, the characters find them for themselves

bools.name: whzQuakeShockWavesDoMoreDamage
bools.comment: when the pressure exceeds the strength of the rocks, one or both rock masses shifts along the fault line, and the shock waves - extending over a much larger area - do much more actual damage than the fault-line shift that started the quake

bools.name: whzQuakeTriggersQuake
bools.comment: one earthquake can cause another if the tremors from the first set off activity along a second nearby fault line

bools.name: whzQuakeAftershocksDays
bools.comment: a quake hardly ever ends with just one tremor - aftershocks occur sporadically for several days as mountain-sized slabs continue to settle

bools.name: whzLightQuakeFewSeconds
bools.comment: a light quake is a shivering or vibrating force through the ground and everything in contact with it, lasting a few seconds or even less, with no directly hazardous effects

bools.name: whzLightQuakeRuinsSpell
bools.comment: a light quake striking a magic-user preparing a spell disrupts his concentration and ruins the spell

bools.name: whzLightQuakeThiefJostled
bools.comment: a thief defusing or avoiding a trap is jostled

bools.name: whzLightQuakeTightropeHalved
bools.comment: a tightrope walker has his chance of success cut in half and falls unless he grabs the rope with a successful Dexterity Check; the DM judges when other concentration or balance tasks are likewise affected

bools.name: whzModQuakeHasLightEffects
bools.comment: a moderate quake has all the effects of a light quake

bools.name: whzModQuakeDislodges
bools.comment: a moderate quake can dislodge a character from a precarious position even if the position is not particularly unstable

bools.name: whzModQuakeToppleNeedsDexStr
bools.comment: a character straddling a limb or branch is toppled from his perch unless he makes both a Dexterity Check (reacting in time) and a Strength Check (grabbing the limb and holding on until the quake subsides)

bools.name: whzModQuakeSpecPointBlankOk
bools.comment: the specialist's -2 penalty does not apply at point blank range

bools.name: whzModQuakeNonSpecRangeStacks
bools.comment: the non-specialist penalties are in addition to the usual penalties for medium and long range

bools.name: whzModQuakeMissSlipFall
bools.comment: and if he misses he will slip and fall as if he was attacking while standing on a slippery horizontal surface

bools.name: whzModQuakeRockfallMudslide
bools.comment: a character at the base of a cliff or severe slope may be set upon by a rockfall or a mudslide depending on the terrain makeup

bools.name: whzModQuakeClimberAlsoAtRisk
bools.comment: of course, anyone climbing either of those surfaces is also subject to these perils

bools.name: whzModQuakeFissureOpens
bools.comment: it is rare but possible for a moderate quake to open a fissure in the ground

bools.name: whzModQuakeFissureFallingDmg
bools.comment: an unfortunate character standing in that exact spot takes falling damage, and possibly abrasion damage as well if he bounces off the sides of the crevasse

bools.name: whzModQuakeFissureCrush
bools.comment: a very unfortunate character, if not killed by the fall, is suffocated or crushed if the two sides of the fissure move toward each other after separating

bools.name: whzSevQuakeDoublesAll
bools.comment: a severe quake has all the effects of a moderate quake, with all penalties and all chances of unfortunate occurrences multiplied by two

bools.name: whzSevQuakeRockfallDoubled
bools.comment: the chance of a rockfall occurring adjacent to a cliff face is twice as great, and so forth

bools.name: whzSevQuakeHitTheGround
bools.comment: during a severe quake the only sensible course of action is to hit the ground (but not from 50 feet in the air), cover your head, and pray to the deity of your choice

bools.name: whzTidalCreatedOnOceanFloor
bools.comment: a tidal wave is created by some cataclysmic occurrence on the ocean floor, such as an earthquake or the eruption of an undersea volcano

bools.name: whzTidalShockAbsorbed
bools.comment: unlike a shock wave in solid matter, the ocean water in the immediate vicinity absorbs the force and passes it on to the surrounding water with relatively little decrease in intensity

bools.name: whzTidalTravelsFar
bools.comment: unless and until something gets in its way, a tidal wave can travel for thousands of miles and still possess enormous force when it hits land

bools.name: whzTidalPrecautionWindow
bools.comment: this much warning may provide time for some precaution - aerial movement, magical protection - but time is at a premium

bools.name: whzTidalRushesInland
bools.comment: a tidal wave may rush inland for several miles before its force is spent

bools.name: whzTidalInlandDiminishes
bools.comment: its velocity diminishes rapidly after it hits land, but several million gallons of water at only 20 miles per hour can still wreak a lot of havoc

bools.name: whzTidalTerrainGoverns
bools.comment: how far inland the wave moves and how rapidly it dissipates depend upon the terrain along the coastline

bools.name: whzTidalCliffSpares
bools.comment: people standing a few hundred yards from the edge of such a cliff might not even get wet

bools.name: whzTidalLowlandFears
bools.comment: people standing there have almost as much to fear as those who live on the coast itself

bools.name: whzTidalPathKills
bools.comment: a character directly in the path of a tidal wave will die - if he survives the buffeting he will at least be knocked unconscious (the section continues onto p. 80 and rides with R487)

flame, no flicker, constant radius; regular lantern light

any artificial light limits long-range visibility for
everyone within the area - the lantern holder cannot make
